# Protected net delivery, intermediary deductions and traced returns

Scope: `contingent_net`. All money fields are integer minor units. Invoice net obligations include recorded historical receipts. Current cash already excludes an in-flight debit. Its result may report both an actual beneficiary credit and a partial return. The return is gross sent minus actual beneficiary credit minus the recorded return charge. Only the net return becomes new customer cash; actual beneficiary credit reduces that invoice's remaining obligation. A trace request or expected return is not money.

An earlier accepted transfer honors its bound bank details. New instructions must use the signed beneficiary direction effective when sent. The bank retains former beneficiaries as registered records and mechanically accepts them; it does not select the customer's current direction. A completed supplier receipt cannot be recovered through this service. A new payment does not cancel a traced old transfer.

## Delivery routes

One protected-net certificate is available. It may be applied to exactly one new remittance, for any positive net amount up to its stated maximum, no later than its inclusive availability minute. Protected delivery immediately debits the requested net amount plus the fixed certificate fee and credits exactly the requested net to the selected beneficiary. Once used, the certificate cannot be split, transferred, cancelled or reused. Protection does not apply to the earlier in-flight remittance.

A standard remittance debits its submitted gross amount immediately. At the scheduled result event, the intermediary's actual fee is deducted from that amount and the remainder reaches the beneficiary. Published possible fees are bounds on the actual fee, not a quote. The fee is part of the gross debit, so it is not debited again when reported. Standard remittances may be submitted only before their result event and at most once per invoice. Their gross amount must exceed the highest published possible fee. Neither the standard debit nor a completed beneficiary receipt can be reversed by another service operation.

After a standard result is final, exact-net top-ups are available at the recorded fixed fee per instruction. A top-up debits its stated net plus fee and credits that exact net. There is no automatic compensation for either a shortfall or an overpayment. A top-up may use the current registered beneficiary even if the first payment used an older one. No new certificate or third-party funding can be obtained.

## Instructions

Unlock `propose_net_delivery`; pass `case_id`, `action`, `data`. The owner approves each exact request.

| Action | Data | Local effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `send` | `invoice_id`, `beneficiary_id`, `route`, `amount_minor` | For route `protected`, amount is desired net; for `standard`, amount is gross sent |
| `topup` | `invoice_id`, `beneficiary_id`, `net_minor` | Send the exact positive net after the standard result, plus the top-up fee |

Local controls enforce available cash, one certificate and route timing. Commercial overpayment, current supplier instructions, continuing private cash reserves and total charges remain service requirements. The total charge includes the original transfer's return fee, the protected fee, actual standard deductions and every top-up fee. `wait_for_update` advances logical time to the next actual event. Queries and errors do not advance it. Deadlines are inclusive.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_net_delivery`

Prepare a protected or standard supplier remittance, or an exact-net top-up after the actual intermediary result.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
